328964770.more_info: Gravel path with gentle grade to wheelchair accessible dock.

328966262.more_info: Follow the Strathcona Parkway to the Paradise Meadows Trailhead in Strathcona Prov. Park.

328967799.more_info: Alias: Wilameno. Trailhead is located about one hour south of Elkford. The trail starts as an ATV route then turns sharply up the hill towards the end. The trail forks at approximately 1km. Right fork leads to Wilema Lake, and the left to Harriett Lake. Trail length: 1.5 km one-way to Wilemena Lake.

328970742.more_info: Follow the Strathcona Parkway to the Paradise Meadows Trailhead in Strathcona Prov. Park. From the trailhead, hike 7 km (approx. 3 hours) to Kwai Lake (passing Battleship, Lady and Croteau lakes along the way).

328974978.more_info: Follow the trail 1 km from Second Champion Lake.

328978034.more_info: Drive 9.8 km along Paul Road from Hwy 5, staying right.Travel 17.7 km on main road (Pinantan-Pritchard) to fork, stay left onto Hyas Lake FSR. Travel 3.6 km on Hyas Lk. Rd, passing Paul Creek FSR on right. Stay left at the fork onto Ware Lk FSR. (About 0.6 km pass Paul Creek FSR). Follow the main road for 4.4 km and stay right. Travel 1.8 and turn right @ the 10km marker. You will pass a yellow gate. Go 0.9km and turn left into a pullout in front of a deactivated road (just before the 11km marker). From here it is about a 500m walk in on a quad trail through a cut block to a fence line. Turn left off of the quad trail and follow the trail/fence line to the lake.

328979392.more_info: Located in Eskers Provincial Park. Turn west off Hwy 97 onto Chief Lake Road. Drive 27 km to and turn north onto Ness Lake Road North. After 1 km you will enter the park and parking area. Follow trail approx. 8km to Butterfly Lake.

328981666.more_info: Within a 30-minute drive of McBride, this lake is host to the popular Lasalle Lakes Recreation Site which includes picnic and camping facilities, a small beach, gravel boat launch, and fishing dock. The Freshwater Fisheries Society of BC stocks rainbow trout in the lake. While motorized boats are not permitted, the lake is small enough (26 hectares) to make fishing from canoe or kayak comfortable. Shoreline fishing is also an option.  Species Present: Rainbow trout. There is shore fishing, picnic sites, a beach, and camping.

328985447.more_info: From Highway 5A near Quilchena, turn on Pennask Lake Road.  Stay right at 22.0 kms on the Pennask Lake Road (left turn goes to Douglas Lake).  Stay left at 27.7 kms (a right leads to Paradise Lake but access is restricted by a locked gate controlled by Douglas Lake Ranch).  At 30.9 kms cross over a cattleguard and at 32.3 kms stay left on the Old Pennask 4x4 Road at the junction with Pennask Lake Road.  A 4x4 is recommended past this point.  Pass under 2 powerlines at 32.4 kms and stay left at 37.9 kms.  RESET ODOMETER.  Lake #2156 is to the right at 1.0 kms and Lake #2158 is on the right at 3.7 kms.  Stay left at 3.8 kms and pass Lake #2157 on the right at 5.6 kms.  At 6.6 kms turn left off of #99 Road.  At 8.3 kms park just off the road at the rustic camping area.  Anglers fishing at Wasley L. often camp here.  Hike approx. 300 m W along a trail to the S central shore of Wasley L.

328985760.more_info: Located in Okanagan Mountain Park. Access to the north boundary parking is via Lakeshore Road from Kelowna. Follow for 15km to the parking area. Access to the south boundary of the park is via Chute Lake Road, and the last few kilometres are very rough and 4WD only. From the north boundary parking, follow the Boulder Trail, CN Trail and Divide Lake Trail to Divide Lake (approx. 9 km). Baker Lake is a further 2 km west of Divide Lake.

328989162.more_info: Drive to Premier Lake and pull into the overflow camping before the main campground. A gate blocks the trail to the lake. From the gate hike along trail for about 15 min. The first lake you come to is Yankee. Follow the trail past Yankee to the next lake which is Canuck.

328989253.more_info: Follow the trail from the Premier Lake overflow camping. Turn right at the first fork in the trail. Hike to Cat's Eye Lake takes ten minutes.

328989616.more_info: Wheelchair accessible dock is approx. 1 km by gravel trail. See security staff at the Rice Lake gatehouse if vehicle access required.

328989635.more_info: Dock 1: Gravel path with 20 cm access lip to dock. Dock 2: Gravel path with 4 cm access lip. Pit toilets.

328989667.more_info: Accessible by 2wd vehicle down 17km of dirt road. Active logging road, CB radio recommended. Access is 68km north of Radium and 36km south of Golden. From HWY 95 in Parson, turn west onto Parson River Crossing Rd. Continue straight, onto Crestbrook Main FSR (Radio controlled road use RR-3). Continue on Crestbrook Main for 6.5km then take a sharp left onto Mitten FSR, following signs for Mitten Lake Recreation Site. Slight left at 14km marker, sign for Mitten.  Joyce Lake is on the left shortly after this turn-off.

328991056.more_info: A circular canoe route with short, user maintained portages, is cleared at the beginning of each summer. Portage through Janice Lake, Dytiscid Lake, Emar Lake, Willowgrouse Lake, Boulder Lake, Club Lake and Next Lake. Parking and camping is available at Janice Lake and Willowgrouse Lake.

328993536.more_info: Short walk to lake from parking on Yellowhead Highway.

328995923.more_info: Gravel pathway to dock. Designated disabled parking spots. Pit toilets.

329014441.more_info: Gravel pathway with 15 cm access lip to a small dock that accomodates 2 anglers. Pit toilet.

329016325.more_info: Very steep slope (23 degrees) to access the dock. No railings or bumpers on part of the dock. Large lip onto the dock.

329058704.more_info: Possibly the most popular lake in the region, and one of the larger (more than 800 hectares) within easy proximity of Prince George (64 kilometres), this lake supports fisheries for wild burbot as well as stocked rainbow trout and kokanee. The northern end of the lake is within Purden Lake Provincial Park, which includes camping, picnic and day-use areas, a great swimming beach, a playground, and hiking trails. The boat launch in the park supports trailered boats, while two docks and a lakeside trail also offer shoreline fishing options, depending on the species. This is the perfect lake for a family trip.    Species Present: Rainbow trout, kokanee, burbot. There is shore-fishing available, a beach, and picnic tables.

329060769.more_info: Directions to fishing dock: Access and parking is from Airmail Road.  There is a short (5-minute) pathway leading from Airmail Road to the dock, which is marked with a Fishing Dock sign at the trailhead.

329060770.more_info: Fishing dock is accessed via the Beaver Trail at the Ice Caves along Hwy 24. Dirt trail to the dock has steep slopes and obstacles.

329060797.more_info: At 3.4 km on Horse Lake Rd N. take left fork onto Horse Lk FSRd. Go 2.4 km turn right onto dirt road Go 0.2 km to field. Turn left and follow this very rough and muddy road to the end. Big rocks at turnaround. Trail to lake from this location.

329060825.more_info: Follow trail from parking lot to

329060848.more_info: Gravel pathway to dock. 12 cm dock access lip. Pit toilets.

329060857.more_info: Follow Highway 24 from Little Fort to Lac des Roche. Turn right onto Wavey Lake road and follow for 9.5 km. Turn left onto 203 RD and travel 2.9 km, stay left at Y, then travel 1.5 km and turn left. Travel 0.5 km to large grassy landing. Lake is 500 meters down ATV trail, turn right at T-intersection.

329064495.more_info: Travel 0.5km down Telkwa High Road from the turn-off from the Yellowhead Hwy. Turn left onto the 2000/ Causqua Forest Service Road and drive for 4 km. Turn right onto a rough road (4WD recommended). After a few kilometers, an ATV or walking is required (approx. 10-min walk). Turn right at the fork, travel 400 m to another fork. Turn left to Duckwing Lake.

329064528.more_info: Hike 3km to lake from parking on Highway 16.

329069272.more_info: From 100 Mile drive to Forest Grove. Go straight at the main intersection for 1.9 km and take the left fork. Travel 0.4 km and go straight on Wilcox Road. Drive 27 km on the main road. Turn right and travel 3.4 km on the main road. Turn right and go 350m to the tree line. Lake is approximately 500m through the trees on an old skid trail.

329069974.more_info: Road access to lake is rough (4WD). Narrow pathway and steep slope onto the dock. Large lip to get onto dock. Pit toilet.

329069999.more_info: Paved pathway with a steep slope to the dock entrance. Pit toilet.

329070032.more_info: From the Buttle Narrows Campground, follow the Partius Lake Trail for 300 metres to the lake.

329085092.more_info: Grass pathway to dock with a 15 cm access lip. Pit toilets.

329086810.more_info: Trailhead from parking lot at base of Green Mountain Road. Trail is 5km to Placid Lake.

329086863.more_info: Trailhead starts from end of Green Mountain Road at Viewing Tower. Trail is 45 minutes to the Foot lake.

329095534.more_info: Hike 9.5 km (300 metres elevation) from the Paradise Meadows Trailhead at Mount Washington Cross-Country Ski Area. Continue past Lake Helen MacKenzie and Hairtrigger Lake to a side trail that branches to the right - this will take you to Circlet Lake.

329095656.more_info: Only a 15-minute drive from Valemount gets you to this small hike-in lake (6.2 hectares) and its quality fishery for stocked rainbow trout. The popular hiking trail of 1.2 kilometres to the lake has had recent improvements. With only a slight gain in elevation of 250 metres, the trail is easy enough to bring in an inflatable craft to fish from should you desire, but options to fish from shore are also available. The Little Lost Lake Recreation Site includes picnic tables, a pit toilet, and swimming in the heat of summer. Species Present: Rainbow trout. Other amenities: picnic tables. Fishery type: Quality. Boat Restrictions: Yes.

329097899.more_info: Gravel path to dock. 18cm dock access lip.

329101309.more_info: Lip on transition to dock. Dock ramp can be quite steep, depending on water levels.

329101319.more_info: Steep gravel pathway from parking lot, with steps down to the dock.  Pit toilets.

329102565.more_info: This jewel of a lake, less than an hour’s drive from Prince George, offers trophy fishing for stocked rainbow trout. While fishing may slow down a bit in summer, you can still get into some great fishing when the fish are “on.” The lake is in Crooked River Provincial Park, just east of the town of Bear Lake. A parking lot can be found off the highway, and from there it’s an easy 200-metre walk to the lake over a set of railroad tracks. As there is not much in the way of shoreline fishing, plan to hand-launch a small boat or inflatable. While lakeside facilities are limited, camping is available in the park. Species Present: Rainbow trout. Other Amenities: shore fishing. Fishery type: Trophy. Boat restrictions: Yes

329102581.more_info: This popular lake (40 hectares) is also just under an hour’s drive from Prince George, and is known for its sandy beaches and great fishing. Small but deep, the lake is stocked with brook trout and rainbow trout. It is managed for a quality fishery – meaning you could hook into some decent-sized fish. To get there, follow Highway 97 north from Prince George for almost 70 kilometres; the turn-off road is not well marked, but watch for the McEwan sign along the rail line (if you cross the tracks, you’ve gone too far). Turn east onto Crystal Lake Road and stay left at the first junction. Continue straight and you will get to the Crystal Lake boat launch area. There is a steep hill, and the road is unpaved. A day-use area includes picnic tables. Shoreline, boats, and kayaks are all good fishing options. Given its 30-metre depths, deep-trolling in cooler waters is one effective option, especially in the summer. Species Present: Rainbow trout, brook trout. Other Amenities: shore fishing, picnic table, beach. Fishery Type: Quality. Boat restrictions: No.

329102635.more_info: For those seeking a more remote wilderness setting, this hike-in lake (16 hectares) is just under an hour’s drive from Prince George, and is stocked with rainbow trout. Following Highway 97 north, access is off Talus Road to Caine Creek Road, both of which are gravel. The trailhead is located near 30.5 kilometres on Caine Creek Road (note the kilometres are not marked). An unmarked trailhead leads approximately 700 metres to the lake. This wilderness location has little in the way of amenities but makes up for it with solitude. As there is no shoreline fishing, a small and portable inflatable, kayak, or canoe is ideal. Species Present: Rainbow trout. Fishery type: Quality

329102641.more_info: This small lake (14 hectares) is close to Crystal Lake, and is stocked with rainbow trout. While shoreline fishing is an option, a small boat will give you more access to fish. Emerald Lake Recreation Site provides rustic camping with tables, pit toilets, and an area to hand-launch a small boat. Travel approximately 70 kilometres north of Prince George along Highway 97. The turn-off road is not well marked, but watch for the McEwan sign along the rail line (if you cross the tracks, you’ve gone too far). Turn east onto Crystal Lake Road and stay left at the first junction. Continue straight and you will get to the Crystal Lake boat launch area. Continue straight past here, and you will come to another junction in the road where the recreation site sign for Emerald Lake directs you left. Continue left and you will get to Emerald Lake.  Species Present: Rainbow trout.  Other amenities: shore fishing, picnic tables. Fishery type: Regional. Boat restrictions: Yes.

329106517.more_info: Located within Bonaparte Prov. Park. The park is accessed via logging roads up Jamieson Creek, which is 25 km north of Kamloops on the Westsyde road. Roads are limited, with access by floatplane and horse.

329123467.more_info: Non-maintained trail located in Elk Lakes Provincial Park.Moderate scrambling and travel through fairly dense undergrowth and occasionally through tangled slide areas is required.  Follow either of the trails that take you to West Elk Pass. A hundred metres west of the Pass boundary the cutline is apparent. This is the most distinct route to Frozen Lake.

329123493.more_info: 500 meter steep hike (90 metres elevation gain) from the road to the first lake.

329123512.more_info: Located in Elk Lakes Provincial Park. Follow the 2 km hiking trail to Upper Elk Lake. Aosta Lower Lake is lcoated off the left-side of the trail as you travel along the southern shore of Upper Elk Lake.

329123584.more_info: 3.7 km hike to Silver Spring Lake number 2 and 3.

329123632.more_info: Located in Elk Lakes Provincial Park. Follow the hiking trail past Lower and Upper Elk Lakes and continue towards Petain Creek Waterfall. Aosta Upper Lake is located on the southern side of the trail, about 500 metres past the south end of Upper Elk Lake.

329148512.more_info: Not stocked, but the lake has a self-sustaining trout population and catch rate is usually good. 26 campsites. Two accessible outhouses. Gravel boat launch. An extensive mountain bike trail network is accessible directly from the campsite.

329176314.more_info: Turn left onto 434 Rd. from Tunkwa Lake Rd. Drive 7.0 km. Cross over powerline. Follow along for 1.5-2.0 km.The pass-through in the fence is at 9.5 km from the start of the 434 road.Park on road and follow trail to lake.

329176324.more_info: Rough access is via the Witches Brook Road off of Highway 97C by driving up the hydro line and continuing past the Gump Lake Recreation Site.

329176336.more_info: Rough access is via the Witches Brook Road off of Highway 97C by driving up the hydro line and continuing past the Gump Lake Recreation Site.

329177889.more_info: 4WD access. Gravel/dirt pathway to fishing dock with many obstacles; dock access lip is 10cm with a steep slope. Pit toilets.

329178000.more_info: Drive 6.8 km up Mount Woodside Forest Service Road to a culvert, where a small, overgrown road on leads off to the left. Stacey Lake is located 300 meters down this road.

329216637.more_info: Gravel pathway to dock.  9 cm dock access lip.

329216650.more_info: From Miller Creek Forest Service Road, turn onto Xenia Branch (rough, 4WD required). Travel 6 km from the start of the branch road to the lake. Depending on your vehicle, you may need to hike part of this road.

329216663.more_info: Drive along Beaverdell State Creek Forest Service Road until you reach Sago Creek. The trail to Collier Lake starts across from Sago Creek. Hike 1 km to Collier, or 2 km to Upper Collier along a moderate trail.

329216664.more_info: Turn left (west) off Highway 16 north of Houston onto Morice Lake Road (just past Finning). Drive 3.8 Kms. and turn right onto Morice-Telkwa Forest Service Road (B4 MAC Forest Road). Drive 1.0 Kms. staying on main road to fork in road. Take left hand fork and follow road over Morice River. Drive 5.2 Kms. to pullout area, just past Moose Enhancement sign on right (just past 6 km marker sign). 300 m trail to lake is on the right hand side of the road along log fence.

329220501.more_info: Drive along Dogtooth-Canyon Forest Service Road until it crosses Cedar Creek. Look for rough access road leading to the small lake (4WD may be required). Park at the Cedar Lake Rec Site. Follow the short trail to the lake.

329220512.more_info: Lake is hard to see from the road. Short hike down a steep bank required to access the lake.

329220525.more_info: A short walk through timber from Spillamacheen Forest Service Road.

329238286.more_info: A trail leads to the lake from the north end of Premier Lake.

329247797.more_info: Dock located in Rec Site. Gravel path with 7cm lip to dock. Pit toilets.

329262690.more_info: Access via Porto Rico Road to Barrett Lake Recreation Site. 4WD-only after first 3km of road.

329272381.more_info: Lying midway between Prince George and Vanderhoof (about a 40-minute drive either way), this small lake (45 hectares) is a paddling favourite among locals. You can catch stocked rainbow trout and wild whitefish. Berman Lake Regional Park features picnic areas with tables, toilets, a dock from which you can launch small boats, and a sandy beach for swimming (complete with change rooms). Norman Lake Road off Highway 16 will get you to the lake. Species Present: Rainbow trout, whitefish. Other amenities: picnic tables, beach

329272482.more_info: About an hour’s drive from Prince George, Square is another lake (12 hectares) located within Crooked River Provincial Park. The Freshwater Fisheries Society of BC stocks the lake with rainbow trout. This is a hike-in-only lake with an easy 30-minute/ 500 meter hike from the parking lot at the western end of Bear Lake. The park offers campsites, a day-use site with flush toilets, picnic tables, and a playground. Species Present: Rainbow trout. Fishery type: Regional. Boat restrictions: Yes

329272509.more_info: Rough 250 meter pathway to dock from recreation site.

329272817.more_info: Kwitzil (a.k.a. Gravelpit) – This small lake (7.3 hectares) is just over 30 minutes’ drive from Prince George. It offers great family fishing for both stocked rainbow trout and eastern brook trout. It is easily accessed off a short, 500-metre gravel road directly from the highway (on the left heading from Prince George). There is a gravel site to launch a small boat or kayak easily, but note that no powered boats are permitted. Shore fishing is also an option. While there are no amenities beyond what is described here, quick access from the city means you can head out even if you only have a couple of hours to spare. Species Present: Rainbow trout, brook trout. Other amenities: Shore fishing available. Fishery type: Family. Boat restrictions: Yes.

329276332.more_info: Proceed 21.0 km on main line of Alex Graham Ross-Forest Service Road. to intersection, stay left. Drive 31.9 km on main road, turn left onto 1700 road (at 52.5 marker) -there is also a Palmer Lake sign. Drive 2.6 km and take right fork. Go 5.5 km to small dirt road on the right (right goes to Palmer Lake). Keep straight on main road for 3.7 km to parking area with map on left. Hike 800 m to lake.

329276620.more_info: From the intersection of highways 20 & 97 drive 71.8 on highway 20 (1.6 km past the Raven Lk turnoff). Turn left off the highway onto Beaumont Road(River ranch access)  Go 1.5 km turn right onto road through field. Go 1.4 km go through the gate. Drive 2.1 km, go through the irrigation ditch. Go .2 km through another gate. Go 1.5 km to the end of the road. Trail is obvious from the end of the road. Hikes takes approx. 20 minutes.

329291831.more_info: Follow Sylvester Road onto Lost Creek FSR. There is turn-off for Terepocki FSR; continue past this along Lost Creek FSR for 1.5 km to a pull-out and walk-in access to Salsbury Lake.

329291884.more_info: The dock is located near the walk-in campsites and is accessed from the lakeside trail, approximately 300m from the day-use parking area. Rolley Lake Park is a predominantly flat wilderness area blanketed with tall trees. The park has a small lake for swimming, fishing and paddling. There are 95 campsites.

329291901.more_info: Wheelchair accessible dock is located off Mill Lake Road.Public flush toilets available.

329291991.more_info: Gravel pathway to dock, with 10 degree slope. Depending on water levels, dock ramp can be steep. Pit toilet.

329303502.more_info: Gravel path with rocks to dock. Dock access lip is 11cm. Pit toilets.

329316091.more_info: Follow trail from Lundbom Lake East Recreation Site, or from Lunbom Grass Area trailhead on Princeton Cutoff Road.

329316127.description: Note 12/01/2025: A gate on Iron Mountain Road from the Highway 5 approach is locked. Access from Highway 97C side is still open.

329320869.more_info: Paved pathway to dock. Steep dock ramp. Bumpers on dock. Flush toilets that are not wheelchair accessible.

329320876.more_info: Alias: Knouff. Driving Directions: Access is off Highway 5 North between Kamloops and Barriere. At Heffley Creek, turn onto Sun Peaks road and follow until junction with Knouff Lake road. Turn onto Knouff Lake road and follow until arriving at recreation site.

329320888.more_info: Rough access is via the Witches Brook Road off of Highway 97C by driving up the hydro line and continuing past the Gump Lake Recreation Site.

329320899.more_info: 5-minute walk down wide gravel path trail from Windy Lake Rec Site to lake. Driving directions: From Clearwater on Yellowhead Hwy 5, turn west onto Old North Thompson Highway Road. Turn north onto Camp Two Road for 1.4 km, then take TFL 18 Road 2 out of Clearwater. Proceed 24.5 km, then turn left onto Road 10. Proceed 13 km and find the site on the left. Use caution: Road 2 is an active log hauling road.

329320906.more_info: No designated path to dock. 20 cm dock access lip. Pit toilets.

329320920.more_info: Wheelchair accessible pit toilet. Dock 1: Wheelchair accessible dirt path with 4cm lip to dock. Wheelchair access to boats. Dock 2: dirt/gravel path with 7cm lip to dock.

329321066.more_info: Drive 9.8 km along Paul Lake Rd., stay right. Travel 19.7 km on main road (Pinantan-Pritchard) to fork, stay left onto Hyas Lake FSR.Follow Hyas Lake road for 3.6 km, stay right. Stay left at 3.8 km towards Hyas Lake Fish Camp Turnoff. Follow Hyas Lake Road for 5.8 km, stay right. Travel .9 km to pullout on right. Hike 250 m down narrow road to lake from pull-out.

329321068.more_info: 4x4 only. Turn on Barriere Town Road at north end of Barriere. Drive 18 km to North Barriere Lake Road and turn left. (Stay straight at 3-way stop in Barriere by High School). Continue on main FSR to 37 km marker, staying left at 33 km. Turn left up Summit Lake Road and travel 1.1 km up steep road. Stay right at intersections. Quad trail to the right before end of road. Hike 60 meters to lake.

329321526.more_info: A circular canoe route with short, user maintained portages, is cleared at the beginning of each summer. Portage through Janice Lake, Dytiscid Lake, Emar Lake, Willowgrouse Lake, Boulder Lake, Club Lake and Next Lake. Parking and camping is available at Janice Lake and Willowgrouse Lake.

329343254.more_info: Dirt pathway with steep sections to dock. No toilets.

329343287.more_info: Located in Eskers Provincial Park. Turn west off Hwy 97 onto Chief Lake Road. Drive 27 km to and turn north onto Ness Lake Road North. After 1 km you will enter the park and parking area. Follow trail approx. 2 km to Camp Lake.

329343334.more_info: Gravel pathway to dock, located close to the parking lot. Pit toilets.

329343463.more_info: Located in Eskers Provincial Park. Turn west off Hwy 97 onto Chief Lake Road. Drive 27 km to and turn north onto Ness Lake Road North. After 1 km you will enter the park and parking area. Follow trail approx. 8km to Butterfly Lake.

329343476.more_info: Located in Eskers Provincial Park. Turn west off Hwy 97 onto Chief Lake Road. Drive 27 km to and turn north onto Ness Lake Road North. After 1 km you will enter the park and parking area. Follow trail approx. 8km to BowLake.

329354723.more_info: From Clearwater go across Clearwater River and turn right onto 2 Forest Service Road. Drive past Coldscaur Lake and stay left onto Boundary Lake Rd (Sign to Mahood Lake). At the 37.5 km sign stay right. Stay on main road for 9.5 km to the 8100 Road. Turn right and drive 0.5 km and turn left. Travel 4.1 km on main road and turn left. Go .9 km, stay right. Travel .8 km, turn right.

329354727.more_info: Located in Schoolhouse Lake Provincial Park. No road access and no trails within the park. The best way into the park is by float plane.

329371063.more_info: The 2 km West Lake L:oop Trail leaves from Bailey Chute Viewing Platform parking lot.

329413147.more_info: Access to Little Blue Lake is on the Moffat Lake Road in Alexandria. Drive along the power lines to the lake.

329431277.more_info: Follow Hwy 97 to Quesnel .Take the West Quesnel exit crossing the Fraser River. Turn right immediately after bridge and drive 500 meters to North Fraser Road. Turn left and drive 96 km towards Nazko. Turn left onto gravel road (Michelle Creek F.S.R. aka. Baezaeko road). Follow main road for 6.3 km. Stay left and travel 2.2 km, stay left and travel about 8 km to Crater Lake sign. Turn left after the 3916 km marker and drive about 1 km. A small road/quad trail heads off to the left. Follow for approx. 1 km. Approximately a 10-minute hike.

329445094.more_info: About 40 kilometres east of Vanderhoof (and 65 kilometres west of Prince George), the lake itself is accessed off Highway 16 at Finmore Road. Drive about six kilometres north, then turn right onto an unnamed road for a short distance before arriving at the Cobb Lake Recreation Site on the northern shore of the lake. This lake (223 hectares) is stocked with both rainbow and eastern brook trout. The recreation site includes a boat launch for trailered boats. There is a voluntary restriction of 20 horsepower in place for boat motors. Some options for shoreline fishing are also available. The site also provides day-use facilities, including picnic tables and pit toilets. Given its easy access, the lake is considered family-friendly. During the heat of summer, fish the drop-off areas where trout are likely to hang out. Species Present: Rainbow trout, brook trout,

329451898.more_info: Access via Stemwinder-Hedley Mtn Forest Service Road.

329459193.more_info: Paved pathway to dock; 5 minute walk from parking lot. Pit toilets.

329459304.more_info: Follow trail that begins at the end of Ida Lane.

329459400.more_info: Located in Okanagan Mountain Park. Access to the north boundary parking is via Lakeshore Road from Kelowna. Follow for 15km to the parking area. Access to the south boundary of the park is via Chute Lake Road, and the last few kilometres are very rough and 4WD only. From the north boundary parking, follow the Boulder Trail, CN Trail and Divide Lake Trail to Divide Lake (approx. 9 km).

329461379.more_info: Located in Okanagan Mountain Park. Access to the north boundary parking is via Lakeshore Road from Kelowna. Follow for 15km to the parking area. Access to the south boundary of the park is via Chute Lake Road, and the last few kilometres are very rough and 4WD only. From the north boundary parking, follow the Boulder Trail, CN Trail and Divide Lake Trail to Divide Lake (approx. 9 km). Norman Lake is just north of Baker Lake, which is a further 2 km west of Divide Lake.

329465469.more_info: Located in Heather-Dina Lakes Prov. Park. Access is via the Parsnip West Forest Service Road (4WD in wet weather). A rough trail leads from Dina #1 to Dina #3 and #7.

329465470.more_info: Drive 10.2 km past Dina Lake Rec Site to 41 km marker. Take first left past 41 km marker, onto Six Mile Bay Forest Recreation Site Rd., and stay left. Drive 0.2 Kms. to fork in road, take left fork. Drive 0.2 kms and turn left onto side road. Proceed 0.4 Kms to small parking area and look for trail on left hand side of road. Trail is steep, 300 m to lake.

329465543.more_info: Located in Heather-Dina Lakes Prov. Park. Access is via the Parsnip West Forest Service Road (4WD in wet weather). A rough trail leads from Dina #1 to Dina #3 and #7.

329467592.more_info: Park in the second parking lot for a shorter walk to the fishing dock. Flush washrooms.

329467594.more_info: Flush and pit washrooms. Designated disabled parking spots. Dock 1: Paved pathway with 4-degree slope. Dock 2: Grass pathway with steep slope and 15 cm lip to access dock.

329467613.more_info:
Wheelchair accessible dock located off Black Franks Drive. Designated disabled parking area.
No public washrooms available.

329467724.more_info: Located in Emar Lakes Provincial Park.

329468842.more_info: Access can be gained to the lake via a path from the edge of the cut block (north shore) through a fringe of trees to the north shore of the lake. Access to the cut block is by a logging road off of Highway 39. The traiul to the lake is 100 - 150. down a steep forested hillside, from the cutblock to the lake.

329473630.more_info: From Dawson Creek Drive West on Hwy 97 for 47 km. turn right on the 275 Road for 18km continue straight onto Stewart Lake FSR for 15km. Road runs straight to the Site. Stewart Lake Recreation Site has 11 camp pads. This site also has a gravel boat launch and a dock.

329494730.more_info: Gravel pathway to dock. 8 cm dock access lip. Pit toilets.

329494736.more_info: Upgraded for increased accessibility in 2022. Path to dock: grass, gravel - Access road: gravel -Parking: gravel lot. Pit toilets. Railings on dock. Wheelchair-accessible picnic benches

329495006.more_info: A circular canoe route with short, user maintained portages, is cleared at the beginning of each summer. Portage through Janice Lake, Dytiscid Lake, Emar Lake, Willowgrouse Lake, Boulder Lake, Club Lake and Next Lake. Parking and camping is available at Janice Lake and Willowgrouse Lake.

329495176.more_info: Gravel pathway with some steep sections (17-degree slope) to dock. No toilets.

329504364.more_info: Gravel pathway with rock obstacles and steep slope to dock. 4cm lip onto the dock. Pit toilet.

329504424.more_info: Access via a short dirt path in Blinkhorn Nature Park.

329518147.more_info: Gravel path with a 10 degree-slope to dock. 13 cm access lip to small dock that can accommodate 2 anglers.

329520002.more_info: Accessible dock located by the rest stop.Pit toilets.

329520037.more_info: Located 42 km northeast of Princeton on Hwy # 40. The campground is just off the the Princeton-Summerland Road. Take Agur Road by turning right off of Hwy # 40 at 40.8 km and follow the road, crossing over the old rail bed. 2.4 km to the camping area from the main road.

329520322.more_info: Gravel pathway with five steps down to the dock. Pit toilets. Dock is close to parking.

329523076.more_info: From Cranbrook, drive south on Hwy 3 to Lumberton and turn right. Drive 3.7 km and turn right at the quarry onto Palmer Bar Rd. Go 0.6 km stay right. Drive 2.1 km and stay left. After 0.4 km turn right onto Kiakho Lakes Rd. Follow this for 1.8 km and stay left. Go another 1.0 km and stay right. Drive 0.3 km and turn right for another 0.6 km to a landing. From this parking spot hike north east down into the canyon for about 300 meters to the south end of the lake.

329523981.more_info: Pathway with some obstacles (roots and rocks) and steep sections to dock. Dock access lip is 15cm. Pit toilets

329524023.more_info: Gravel pathway to dock is partially eroded with large rocks in path. 10 cm dock access lip. Pit toilets. Located in Norbury Provincial Park.

329524100.more_info: Drive to Premier Lake and pull into the overflow camping before the main campground. A gate blocks the trail to the lake. From the gate hike along trail for about 15 min. The first lake you come to is Twin Lakes (Yankee).

329524502.more_info: East dock: Paved pathway. Flush toilets.

329532570.more_info: Follow the trail for 300 metres from the Alice Lake praking lot. You will pass Edith Lake.

329532663.more_info: Follow the trail for 200 metres from the Alice Lake parking lot.

329534142.more_info: Access to the site is off Highway 1, east of Kamloops. Travel along Barnhartvale Road until the intersection with Robins Range Road. Turn right onto Robins Range Road. Follow Robbins Range Road until the intersection with Campbell Range Road. Turn right onto Campbell Range Road. Follow Campbell Range Road until the intersection with Scuitto Lake Forest Service Road. Turn right onto the Scuitto Lake Forest Service Road. Travel approximately 12 km until to reach the Scuitto Lake Recreation Site. Stay on the main road and continue past the Scuitto Lake Recreation Site. The road parallels Scuitto Lake. Once past Scuitto Lake the road branches again. Take the right hand branch road and travel over the cattleguard and follow the road to another un-named intersection. Taking a left brings you to the entrance of the Campbell Lake Recreation Site.

329534172.more_info: From the far end of Roche Lake Rec Site take the rough road to the left ( not the Black/Bog Rd but the next one). Go 0.2 km stay left. Go 0.9 km stay right crossing under powerline. Go 2.2 km and stay right. Go 2.8 km to lake (rough road).

329534206.more_info: Drive 24 km on Pillar Lake Road (Shuswap-Chase Road). until you reach Charcoal Road (China Valley) and turn left. Drive on main road for 13.9 km to Blanc Road. Turn left. Go 3.8 km, crossing a creek at a switchback and turn right onto Bryden Road. Travel 2.3 km on main road (passing Bryden Pement Lakes Trail on GPS) and stay right. Travel 0.4 km to quad trail on right side of road in logging block. This is access to lake. Hike down quad trail for 350 meters. Note that Bryden Pement Trail also goes to the lake (600 m hike).

329534292.more_info: Turn left at the Roche Lake Rec Site. Go 3.8 kms on rough road to lake on right (Black is the first lake on right at 0.8). Bog is the next lake.

329539677.more_info: Turn off Highway 27 onto Fish Lake Rd. Turn left onto a pullout, before the turn-off to Echo Lake Bible Camp. A trail leads 250 metres to the lake.

329547759.more_info: About a 45-minute drive south of Prince George, this lake (42 hectares) receives stocked rainbow trout. To get to the lake, turn left off Highway 97 about 11 kilometres south of Stone Creek onto the gravel Camp Creek Road. Drive 900 metres to the intersection, stay right, and then drive another 5.1 kilometres to the lake. A small gravel boat launch is located at the southern end of the lake, but no other facilities exist. Species Present: Rainbow trout. Fishery type: Regional.

329547900.more_info: Dock 1: Closest to the parking lot. Gravel pathway with steep sections. Dock 2: 15 minute walk from parking lot. Pathway with very steep sections and root/rock obstacles.

329619114.more_info: This small, shallow lake (124 hectares) is about 30 kilometres northwest of Valemount. It includes the small, day-use Shere Provincial Recreation Site with pit toilets and easy foot-access to the lake. The lake supports a quality fishery for stocked eastern brook trout, which are best fished from a canoe or kayak. This lake offers breathtaking views of the nearby Rockies. From Valemount, proceed north on the Yellowhead Highway 5 for eight kilometres, and turn left onto Blackman Road. Continue for 10 kilometres and turn left onto Old Tete Jaune Cache Road. Proceed 12 kilometres to Croydon Forest Service Road, another 11 kilometres to Shere Lake Road on the right, and one final kilometre to the site. Given its more complicated driving access, you can be sure this lake will not be crowded. Species Present: Brook trout Lake.  Other amenities: picnic tables. Fishery type: Quality. Boat restrictions: Yes.

329650841.more_info: Drive north through Blue River; go about _ km past the Blue River Bridge, to Blueberry Road. Turn left and stay left on the main (lower) road for 3.1 km to road junction (White River). There is an old skidder road across from this junction on the left-hand side. Twin No. 2 (McCormick) is 50 m down this trail to the left. From Twin  No. 2 (McCormick) follow the swampy meadow to the right for about 400 m to get to Twin  No. 1.

329663993.more_info: Located within Denison-Bonneau Prov. Park. The trailhead of the Denison-Bonneau Lakes Trail is located on Bonneau FSR. Hiking distance: 9km.

329676313.more_info: Wheelchair accesible dock located at the end of Bear Hill Road. Flush washrooms.

708021500.more_info: This very small lake (1.6 hectares) sits within Mount Robson Provincial Park, an hour’s drive from Valemount. The stocked rainbow trout in this lake can be fished via kayak or small inflatable, or from shore. You can access this lake immediately off the highway at a rest stop. Species Present: Rainbow trout. Other amenities: picnic tables, shore fishing. Fishery type: regional. Boating restrictions: Yes
